This movie had great production value and competent direction. I think it got all this praise because it just didn't suck and people were desperate for a new good Star Wars. Personally, I don't mind the rehashing and fanservice, apart form the new Death Star. Why did the First Order do this? That plan didn't work out pretty well the last two times. Aside from that, I actually enjoyed the movie, but wouldn't rate it very high, to me it's somewhere between the originals and the prequels. On the positive side: Abrams put in way more effort than Lucas did with all of the prequels combined and the plot makes more sense than that of the Star Trek reboot (which had insanely good casting). The Force Awakens was held back by its characters and plot convinces. I found actually all characters to be boring or even annoying.

  • Finn: He was a janitor? So why did he wear the typical Stormtrooper Uniform? Why was he on an away mission? Why did it take him so long to realise that the First Order are the bad guys? He grew up in that environment and still managed to sound like he grew up in the Bronx. He didn't have anything that made him interesting, apart form being the token black guy, there was no ark, no inner conflict. Basically, you could have left him out of the movie entirely, without changing the plot or anyones relations.

  • Poe: He was a very skilled and likable character, that's it. I'm wondering will he be the Wedge Antilles type or will he be part of the new main character trio? Actually I don't know from the too short time we've seen him. If you'd asked me, he should be more cocky, he's just too much of a nice guy. Also, in this movie you could have replaced him with generic action guy who dies on his mission. His and Finns friendship feels forced, they just became best buddies in the five minutes that had together on screen.

  • Kylo: I couldn't take him seriously, "Can you make the pain go away?", what kind of bullshit line was this? Darth Vader had no depth whats so ever in A New Hope, but as Luke discovered more about him, his character grew deeper. And he was intimidating from the moment he walked on screen. Kylo on the other hand was too skinny and small and you couldn't understand a word he said. Also, he was insanely inconstant, in one scene he could block a laser blaster in the next he had trouble fighting Finn, who has no sensitivity for the Force and no training. Kylo isn't a complex character, he has no inner conflict, he's just whiny, unlike Vader, who grew from being menacing to someone who's struggling with himself, without being a bickering weakling. Judging this movie by it's villain, it is a terrible one. It has been a while since watching the prequels, so I won't compare him to Anakin.

  • Snoke: The Emperor was just hinted at in A New Hope, in Empire we see Darth Vader kneeling before him and in Jedi Ian McDiarmid portrayals him perfectly. What did we get with Snoke, some disfigured guy everybody was blithely standing in front of him. Remember how terrified the empirical officer was when Darth Vader told him that the Emperor would personally oversee the completion of the new Death Star? With Snoke nobody seemed to bother. Also "Palpatine had a big hologram and was disfigured, let's make Snokes hologram biggerer and him disfigurererder".

  • The Rest of the Bad guys: They all were generic bad guys and I don't remember any of their names, except of that Cylon Toaster girl, which I think got Boba Fetted.

  • Han: If I were to ignore the old movies, he was just a random old dude. Ford played him very good, I have really nothing else to say, like Obiwan he sacrificed himself, but it didn't make sense to me. Darth Vader and Obiwan had history and it was very clearly hinted at, and he let Darth Vader kill him, so Luke could escape, besides it had an impact on the whole story and on Luke himself. Solos death just happened and everybody moved on. (Will there be a Han Solo ghost at the end of Episode IX on Endor second edition, when the new Rebellion, err Resistance celebrates with much cuter Ewok lookalikes?)

  • Leia: Why was she in that movie? Did she have anything to do but look troubled?

  • Rey: The universally loved one, both from critics, people and within the movie. Everybody fell in love with her instantly, Finn, Chewy, Han, BB-8 and even Kylo. He said he could show her the Darkside of the Force. She had a heart of gold and was completely selfless, flawless and tried constantly saving and helping everybody. She saved Finn multiple times and refused an offer of food for BB-8. While we're at it, why does she understand Android? How stupid is this. Yeah maybe in all the years scavenging she picked up a few mechanical skills, but she could understand BB-8 right from the get go. She was instantly in tune with the Force and could resist mind read, could pull of a Jedi mind trick (this scene reminded me of Austin Powers and Will Ferrell), could grab a Light Saber from a pretty good distance away and had uber fighting skills. And not just this, she learned flying the Millennium Falcon within mere minutes and out maneuvered trained Tie Fighter Pilots. And don't get at me with "but Luke was a good pilot, too". Yes he was, that's all he could do in the first movie and it was hinted at multiple times (back home we see his T16, Obiwan says he's a good pilot, in a mission briefing he says he killed womp rats from his T16 and he hit a thermal exhaust port with heat seeking missiles). Luke gets into trouble throughout the whole movie and other people need to help him. Obiwan defends him against the Tusken Raiders and in the Cantina, Leia leads them out of the cell block and Han shots at Vader in the trench scene. Rey learns the ways of the Force all by herself, learns to fly all by herself and gets herself out of trouble all by herself and all of that in just one movie and all without any trying, it's like Yoda said "do or do not there is no try". Some people suggested that she maybe had secret training. But by whom and when? Luke was the last Jedi and she was left on Jakku as a very young girl. Rey is never at risk and has no stakes, she is never conflicted about what she is doing. Basically she is a video game character.

  • "Plot": It is littered with plot conveniences. Right as Rey and Finn leave Tatoo… Jakku Han and Chewy show up, Poe runs into the only rebellious Stormtrooper, after the new new Death Star was destroyed R2D2 wakes up and has the map that leads to Skywalker, Maz Kanata lives on a neighboring planet to Coruscant, so the main characters can see how the First Order destroys the Republic capital from not too far away. There are so many things wrong with this scene. Were there no defenses? Alderaan was a peaceful planet and Leia said they had no weapons. All planets were just by chance in view of each other. After the First Oder destroyed Coruscant they decided to invade the local planets? Why not destroy them, too? Why the need to invade them at all, Maz Kanatas planet didn't seem very important. Maz Kanata gave Rey Lukes old blue Lightsaber, the one that Anakin constructed. Which is actually impossible. In Empire Luke was fighting Vader and Vader cut of his hand and he lost the Lightsaber, hence he built a new one. Some reviews said the movie would end with a cliffhanger and that we would get more questions than answers. Actually this whole Luke scene at the end felt more like a after credit scene than anything else. I don't have any questions, I'm just baffled. The reviews said all these nitpicks will probably be explained in the upcoming movies, that's just an excuse. Leaving things open or ambiguous is one thing, but doing some random stuff and hoping the sequels will fix it is another.

While I really wanted Star Wars sequels, they don't make any sense at all. There were great stories in the EU (Kotor 1&2 being my favorites), but the core plot of Star Wars happened in Episodes 1 - 6. The first three movies told the story of the Empires rise, the original movies was the story of it's fall. And it is the character story of Anakin Skywalker, told from Obiwans and Lukes perspective, how he raise to power, how he was seduced by the Darkside and how he found redemption. Since Anakin is dead and the Empire is defeated, the whole story arc is done. Trying to build upon that is near impossible. I was very nitpicky and very negativ, the reason is, this movie doesn't need more praise. That being said, I had a good time watching it, these were just some thoughts I had afterwards. I'm not sure if I will rewatch it (I've seen the prequels just once). In the end it felt like a very good fan made movie and I think every Star Wars fan should see.

TL;DR: The characters were boring, all of them, the plot didn't make sense, still enjoyed the movie.

I liked most of the characters, and I thought the writing was pretty good, but past that, the plot kinda sucked. It was just Episode IV rehashed with some of the tropes moved around a bit so the filmmakers thought the audience couldn't tell. Hate on me all you want for saying this, but at least the prequel films had original plots. There was just so much going on and, despite the bland characters, the overall plots to the films were very interesting to me. Yes, even the stuff about trade routes and negotiations. Maybe it's my background in political science (I have a degree in it) but I thought all that stuff presented a more intellectual story for a more intelligent audience. Sometimes you don't need constant action to tell a sci-fi/fantasy story.

After digesting the movie I did like it for the most part. However, they really didn't do anything interesting in the plot, same rehash of story from A New Hope.
